```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4, dpi = 110)
```

```{r setup}
library(svid)
```

## The data

`andong` holds Sentinel-2A surface reflectance at 1,790 reference points over
32 dates of 2022, covering rice paddies, pepper fields and plastic-covered
greenhouses.

```{r}
data(andong)
d <- svid_from_table(andong,
                     bands = c(B = "B02", G = "B03", R = "B04", N = "B08"),
                     response = "class", id = "point_id", epoch = "date",
                     coords = c("x", "y"), group = "parcel",
                     sensor = "sentinel2")
d
```

The printout reports two things that matter later: the classes are strongly
imbalanced, and the 1,790 pixels fall into far fewer independent parcels.

```{r, fig.height = 4.5}
svid_plot_profiles(d, "(N - R) / (N + R)")
```

## Generating and pruning a pool

```{r}
pool <- svid_generate(svid_grammar(d$bands, max_depth = 1))
pool
```

Most of those expressions are not distinct features.

```{r}
pool <- svid_prune(pool, d)   # numerical stages use a 500-sample subsample
svid_redundancy(pool)
```

```{r}
svid_plot_redundancy(pool)
```

The classes are worth inspecting directly. Every member of a class is the same
feature written differently, so any difference in their scores is an artefact.

```{r}
head(attr(pool, "members")[lengths(attr(pool, "members")) > 1], 2)
```

## Screening, then modelling

Fitting a model per index is wasteful when the pool is large. Screen first.

```{r}
sc <- svid_separability(pool, d)
head(sc, 5)
short <- svid_shortlist(sc, n = 8)
```

```{r}
fit <- svid_evaluate(short, d,
                     resampling = svid_resample(d, "group", folds = 5),
                     n_seeds = 2, baselines = c("raw_bands", "ndvi"))
fit
```

## Inference

A ranking is only meaningful if the differences exceed the noise.

```{r}
svid_tied(fit)
```

```{r}
svid_stability(fit, d, max_classes = 5)
```

```{r}
head(svid_compare(fit), 5)
```

## Reporting

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- svid_result(pool, fit, d)
svid_report(res, "svid-report.html", pool = pool, fit = fit, data = d)
```
